item.title: Inventory Planning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Safety stock, reorder point, EOQ and a recommended reordering policy, computed from your posted item ledger entries and written to the standard Business Central fields. Free and open source.

Read the documentation View the source

The problem it solves

Business Central's planning engine is capable and correct. It also does exactly what your item cards tell it to — and on most systems that means Safety Stock Quantity is empty, Reorder Point was typed in at go-live by somebody estimating, and Reorder Quantity is a round number nobody has revisited since.

The engine executes those guesses faithfully. The business absorbs the result as stockouts on the items that matter and dead stock on the ones that don't.

What it calculates

CalculatorProducesWrites to
Safety stock Buffer covering demand and lead-time variability at your service level Item Safety Stock Quantity
Reorder point Demand during lead time, plus safety stock Item Reorder Point
EOQ Wilson economic order quantity, capped and order-modifier aware Item Reorder Quantity or Order Multiple
Maximum inventory Order-up-to level for Maximum Qty. items Item Maximum Inventory
Policy advisor Demand classification and a recommended reordering policy Item Reordering Policy (opt-in)

Why this one

It writes standard fields

There is no parallel data model. Standard planning, requisition worksheets and MRP consume the results immediately with nothing to reconfigure — and if you ever uninstall the app, the values stay on your items.

It shows its working

Every calculation records the demand statistics behind it, the lead time and where that lead time came from, the service level and Z-score, the costs, the previous value and the reasoning. When somebody asks why an item's reorder point is what it is, the answer is one click away — months later.

It tells you when to doubt it

Very few planning tools admit their own limits. This one warns you when recent demand has diverged from the historical window, when Stockkeeping Units mean the planning engine reads a different value than the item card, and when an item's demand is too intermittent for the underlying statistics to be trusted.

You review before you commit

The Planning Worksheet shows current versus proposed values side by side for any filtered set of items, tells you how many lines change the reorder point by more than 25%, and applies only the lines you tick. Applying re-runs the calculators through their validated, logged path — nothing is blind-copied from the preview.

How your team uses it

  • One item — from the Item Card, while you are looking at it
  • A category or a vendor's range — from the Item List, on your current filter or selection
  • A reviewed rollout — through the Planning Worksheet
  • Unattended — a nightly Job Queue entry, created for you from the setup page
  • At planning time — optionally, values computed live during a planning run rather than read from the item

What it does not do

It calculates at item level. Per-location planning through Stockkeeping Units, ABC-driven service levels and exception workbenches are outside its scope — and the app tells you, in the calculation note, when an item has SKUs so you are never left wondering why a value "isn't working".

It is descriptive statistics over posted history, not forecasting and not machine learning. That is a deliberate choice: every number it produces can be traced back to transactions you can open.

Requirements and licence

  • Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (v28) or later, cloud
  • Free. MIT licensed. Source at github.com/GmsoftLtd/bc-inventory-planning
  • Two permission sets ship with the app: one for planners, one for administrators
Talk to us Getting started

item.title: Documentation
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Everything you need to configure and run the safety stock, reorder point, EOQ and reordering policy calculators for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

New here?

Start with Getting started — install, permissions, the five setup values that matter, and calculating your first item.

Guides

  • Getting started Install, assign permissions, review the defaults and calculate your first item.
  • Setup reference Every setup field, its default, and what changing it does.
  • Running the calculators Per item, in bulk from the Item List, and on a nightly schedule.
  • Planning Worksheet Preview current versus proposed values and apply only what you select.
  • Calculation log Read the audit trail and set a retention policy.
  • Per-item controls Exclude items from planning and override the service level per item.

Reference

  • Troubleshooting Result codes, warnings, and what to do about each one.
  • FAQ Formulas, methodology, data handling and scope.

How the app works, briefly

All four calculators read one shared statistics engine, so they agree on what "demand" and "lead time" mean for a given item.

Demand is sales, netted against same-day returns, measured across every calendar day in the history window. In manufacturing companies you can also count production and assembly consumption, so purchased components are planned from real usage rather than from sales they never appear in.

Lead time is resolved from purchase receipt history where it exists — the only source that also yields variability — then from the item's Lead Time Calculation, then from a fallback you set. Safety stock and reorder point always use the same resolution, so the two can never disagree.

Results are written to the standard item planning fields. There is no parallel data model, and standard planning consumes them with no further configuration.

Formulas

Safety stock, covering variability in both demand and lead time:

SS = Z × √( LT × σD² + D² × σLT² )

Reorder point:

ROP = (average daily demand × lead time) + safety stock

Economic order quantity, the Wilson formula:

EOQ = √( 2 × D × S / H )

Where D is annual demand, S the ordering cost and H the annual holding cost per unit. Full derivations and the reasoning behind the defaults are in the FAQ.

Still stuck?

Contact support — we answer within 2 business days. The app is open source, so you can also read the calculation code or raise an issue on GitHub.

item.title: Support
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Talk to the people who build the app. No ticket portal login, no account manager in between.

We reply within 2 business days.

Support hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-18:00 UK time. Questions received outside those hours are answered on the next working day.

How to reach us

ChannelDetailsBest for
Email support@gmsoft.co.uk Most questions. Attach a screenshot and we can usually answer in one reply.
Telephone +44 7771 313713 Urgent problems, or anything easier to explain out loud.
Contact form Send us a message If you would rather not use email directly.
Issue tracker GitHub issues Bug reports and feature requests you are happy to have in public.

Before you contact us

Two things answer most questions faster than we can:

  • Troubleshooting — every result code and warning, and what to do about each
  • FAQ — formulas, methodology, data handling and scope

What to include

For anything about a calculated value, these four things usually contain the whole answer:

  1. The item number
  2. A screenshot of the calculation log entry for that item — it carries every input that produced the result
  3. Your Inventory Planning Setup page
  4. What you expected the value to be, and why

For an error, add the full message text and roughly when it happened.

What we support

The app is free and MIT licensed, and we support it properly: questions about how it works, help interpreting results, bug reports, and guidance on configuring it for your range.

Advice on your wider planning setup, per-location planning, data cleanup or custom development sits outside app support — but we do that work too. Ask, and we will tell you which side of the line your question falls on.

Reporting a security issue

Email support@gmsoft.co.uk with the details rather than opening a public issue, and we will respond directly.

item.title: Getting started
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
From install to your first calculated item in about ten minutes.

1. Install

Install from AppSource. On installation the app creates its setup record with working defaults, registers itself under Manual Setup, and registers its calculation log with the standard Retention Policy module.

Nothing is calculated and no item is touched until you ask for it.

2. Assign permissions

Permission setGive it toGrants
GSO - User
Inventory Planning - User		 Planners, buyers Run the calculators, use the worksheet, read the log and setup
GSO
Inventory Planning		 Administrators The above, plus editing setup and maintaining the log

Anyone who runs standard planning while the optional dynamic provider is enabled needs at least GSO - User.

3. Review the setup

Search for Inventory Planning Setup. The defaults suit a distributor with a year of clean history:

SettingDefaultChange it if…
Demand History Window (Days)365Your range turns over much faster, or you have less than a year of data
Min Demand Observations20Your items sell on fewer than 20 distinct days a year
Default Service Level %95Your business targets a different availability level
Ordering Cost (S)50You know your real cost of raising and receiving one order
Holding Rate0.25Your cost of capital and storage differs from 25% a year
If you manufacture or assemble, turn on “Count Consumption as Demand”.

Without it, a component consumed by production shows no demand at all, because it is never sold. Every purchased component will report Zero Demand and no values will be produced.

The full field-by-field reference is in Setup reference.

4. Calculate one item you know well

Open an item whose demand you could describe from memory — that is what makes the first result meaningful.

Item Card → Inventory Planning → Calculate All Planning Values.

The app runs everything in dependency order: policy advice, then safety stock, then reorder point (fed the fresh safety stock, not the stored one), then EOQ, then maximum inventory. It reports what it found and why.

Now open Item Card → Inventory Planning → Calculation Log and read the entry. It shows the demand statistics, the lead time and its source, the Z-score, and the previous value. If the numbers look wrong, this is where you find out why — usually the history window or the demand definition, not the arithmetic.

5. Roll out to a range

Do not start with a bulk apply. Use the Planning Worksheet:

  1. Item List → Inventory Planning → Planning Worksheet
  2. Load Items, filtered to one item category or one vendor
  3. Read the variance message — it tells you how many lines move the reorder point by more than 25%. Check those first.
  4. Tick the lines you accept, then Apply Selected

6. Schedule it

Inventory Planning Setup → Create Job Queue Entry creates a daily 03:00 recurring entry, on hold so you can review it. Set it to Ready when you are satisfied.

See Running the calculators for the parameter values that control what each scheduled run does.

7. Set a log retention policy

The log grows by one row per item per calculator per run. Search for Retention Policies, add one for the GSO Calculation Log table, and set a period — 90 days is a sensible start. Without a policy, nothing is ever deleted.

Next: Setup reference · Troubleshooting

item.title: Setup reference
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Search for Inventory Planning Setup, or find it under Manual Setup. One page configures all four calculators.

General

These settings apply to every calculator.

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Demand History Window (Days)365 Calendar days of history to analyse, ending on the work date. Range 30–1095. A shorter window reacts faster to change but is noisier; a longer one is stabler but lags.
Min Demand Observations20 Minimum number of days with demand before a result is produced. Below this the item reports Insufficient Demand Data. Minimum 3. This counts days, not transaction lines.
Round Up Results to Whole UnitsYes Round results up to whole units. Turn off for items measured in kilograms, litres or metres.
Log Calculation HistoryYes Write an entry to the calculation log for every calculation. Leaving this on is what makes results auditable.
Skip Make-to-Order ItemsYes Skip items whose replenishment is make-to-order. Their supply is driven by the order that demands them, not by a reorder point.
Fallback Lead Time (Days)7 Used when neither receipt history nor the item's Lead Time Calculation yields a lead time.
Count Consumption as DemandNo Count production and assembly consumption as demand alongside sales. Turn this on in manufacturing companies, or purchased components will report zero demand.
Trend Warning Threshold % (0 = off)30 Warn in the calculation note when recent demand deviates from the window average by more than this. Set 0 to disable.

Safety stock

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Default Service Level %95 Probability of not stocking out during a replenishment cycle. Range 70–99.99. Can be overridden per item.
Write Safety Stock to ItemYes Turn off to calculate and log without writing anything to items — useful while you are evaluating.
Service level is not linear in cost.

Moving from 95% to 99% roughly doubles the buffer. Raise it for the items where a stockout is expensive, not across the board — that is what the per-item override is for.

Reorder point

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Add Safety Stock to Reorder PointYes Include the freshly calculated safety stock in the reorder point, rather than the value stored on the item.
Write Reorder Point to ItemYesTurn off to preview only.
Set Policy to Fixed Reorder Qty. when NoneYes Give items with no reordering policy one, so the calculated reorder point actually does something. Suppressed for an item when the advisor recommends a different policy.
Write Maximum Inventory (ROP + EOQ) for Maximum Qty. ItemsYes Set the order-up-to level for items on the Maximum Qty. policy.

EOQ

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Ordering Cost (S)50 Cost of placing one order — administration, receiving, inspection — in your local currency. This is the single input most worth getting right.
Holding Rate0.25 Annual cost of holding one unit as a fraction of unit cost. 0.25 means 25% a year, covering capital, storage, insurance and obsolescence. Range 0–1.
Maximum EOQ (Months of Demand)6 Cap on the result. Stops a cheap, high-volume item from ordering two years of stock. Minimum 0.5. When the cap binds, the result code is Cap Applied.
EOQ Write TargetReorder Quantity Or Order Multiple, if you would rather the planning engine round order sizes than fix them.
Unit Cost SourceLast Direct Cost Or Standard Cost or Unit Cost. Pick the one your items actually populate.
Write EOQ to ItemYesTurn off to preview only.

Policy advisor

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Intermittent ADI Threshold1.32 Average Demand Interval above which demand counts as intermittent. The standard Syntetos–Boylan value.
Erratic CV-Squared Threshold0.49 Squared coefficient of variation above which demand size counts as erratic. Also Syntetos–Boylan.
Treat Shelf Life as Maximum Qty.Yes Items with an Expiration Calculation are steered to the Maximum Qty. policy so standing stock is capped.
Auto-Update Item Reordering PolicyNo Whether an applied advice run writes the recommended policy to the item. Off by default. Recommendations are logged either way — turn this on only once you trust the advice.

Auto-update only ever writes Fixed Reorder Qty., Maximum Qty. or Lot-for-Lot. It never flips an item to Order automatically: that is a sourcing decision, not a statistical one.

Planning engine integration

FieldDefaultWhat it does
Supply Values at Planning Time (Dynamic)No Supplies freshly calculated values to the planning engine during a planning run, instead of relying on whatever the last batch run wrote to the item.
Verify the dynamic provider on a sandbox first.

Run a regenerative plan for one item, confirm the requisition line reflects the calculated values, and check that a Dynamic Supply entry appears in the calculation log. Real Stockkeeping Units are never modified, items that cannot be calculated fall back to their stored values, and order modifiers stay under the planning engine's control.

Actions on this page

  • Create Job Queue Entry — a daily 03:00 recurring entry, created on hold for you to review
  • Planning Worksheet — opens the worksheet
  • Calculation Log — opens the log

Next: Running the calculators · Per-item controls

item.title: Running the calculators
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Four ways to run: one item, a filtered set, a reviewed worksheet, or unattended on a schedule.

One item — from the Item Card

Item Card → Inventory Planning

ActionWhat it does
Calculate All Planning ValuesEverything, in dependency order
Calculate Safety StockSafety stock only
Calculate Reorder PointReorder point only
Calculate EOQEOQ only
Advise Reordering PolicyClassifies demand and recommends a policy
Calculation LogOpens the log filtered to this item

Each action reports its result and its reasoning. Whether the value reaches the item depends on the matching Write … to Item switch in setup.

Why “Calculate All” is not just the four actions in a row.

It runs them in dependency order — policy advice, safety stock, reorder point, EOQ, maximum inventory — and feeds the reorder point the freshly calculated safety stock rather than whatever is stored on the item. Running the individual actions out of order can build a reorder point on a stale safety stock.

It also suppresses the “Set Policy to Fixed Reorder Qty. when None” default for an item whose advice recommends something else, so one run never stamps a policy its own advice contradicts.

A filtered set — from the Item List

Item List → Inventory Planning

ActionWhat it does
Planning WorksheetOpens the preview worksheet
Calculate All (Selected/Filtered Items)Runs everything and applies, after confirming the item count
Advise Policy (Selected/Filtered Items)Classifies demand and logs recommendations

Scope: if you have selected more than one row, the selected rows win. Otherwise the current filter on the list defines the scope. Non-inventory, blocked and excluded items are skipped automatically.

Long runs commit every 100 items, so an interrupted run keeps the work already done.

Bulk actions apply immediately.

They write to items after a single confirmation. If you want to see the numbers before they land, use the Planning Worksheet instead — that is what it exists for.

Unattended — Job Queue

Inventory Planning Setup → Create Job Queue Entry creates a recurring entry that runs every day at 03:00, created on hold. Review the schedule, then set it to Ready.

The Parameter String on the entry selects what runs:

ValueRuns
ALL (default, also used when empty)Everything, in dependency order
SAFETYSTOCKSafety stock only
REORDERPOINTReorder point only
EOQEOQ only
ADVISORPolicy advice only

Create several entries with different parameters and schedules if that suits you — for example policy advice weekly, safety stock nightly.

Scheduled runs apply to every eligible item.

Protect any item whose planning values a person maintains by hand: tick Exclude from Inventory Planning on the item card.

At planning time — the dynamic provider

Optionally, the app can supply freshly calculated values to the planning engine during a planning run, instead of relying on whatever the last batch run wrote. Off by default; see Setup reference before enabling it.

Next: Planning Worksheet · Troubleshooting

item.title: Planning Worksheet
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Current versus proposed values, side by side, for any filtered set of items — with selective apply. The safest way to roll the app out.

Open it from Item List → Inventory Planning → Planning Worksheet, from the setup page, or by searching for Inventory Planning Worksheet.

How to use it

  1. Load Items — choose a filter on item number, item category or vendor. Every matching inventory item is calculated as a preview. Nothing is written.
  2. Read the variance message. It reports how many lines change the reorder point by more than 25%, so a large worksheet can be triaged instead of read line by line.
  3. Review the columns, starting with those large movers.
  4. Tick the lines you accept. Select All and Clear Selection help with big sets.
  5. Apply Selected — confirms the count, then applies.
Applying is not a copy of the preview.

The calculators re-run through their validated, logged path, so an apply is exactly equivalent to running each item individually. Applied lines refresh their “current” columns in place and are deselected, so you can see the effect without reloading.

Reading the columns

ColumnShows
Demand PatternSmooth, Erratic, Intermittent or Lumpy — see how patterns are classified
Current / Recommended PolicyThe item's reordering policy today, and what the advisor suggests
Current / Proposed Safety StockSafety Stock Quantity, before and after
Current / Proposed Reorder PointReorder Point, before and after
Current Reorder Quantity / Proposed EOQReorder Quantity today, and the calculated economic order quantity
Current / Proposed Maximum InventoryThe order-up-to level for Maximum Qty. items
SS / ROP / EOQ Result CodeThe outcome of each calculator — see Troubleshooting
NoteThe advisor's reasoning, plus any trend, SKU or lumpy-demand warning

What to look at first

  • Lines the variance message flagged. A reorder point that moves more than 25% is either a real correction or a data problem. Both are worth ten seconds.
  • Result codes that are not OK. An Insufficient Demand Data or Zero Demand line produced no value, so ticking it achieves nothing.
  • Notes containing warnings. Trend warnings mean the history is not describing the present. SKU notices mean planning reads a different value than the item card.
  • Policy changes. A recommended policy that differs from the current one changes how the planning engine behaves, not just by how much — review these before anything else.
Nothing on this page writes to items until you choose Apply Selected.

Loading, sorting, filtering and selecting are all safe. You can close the worksheet at any point and nothing will have changed.

A sensible rollout

Work through one item category or one vendor's range at a time rather than the whole catalogue. Each pass gives you a feel for whether the setup values — particularly the history window, the service level and the ordering cost — suit that part of your range, and you can adjust before the next pass.

Next: Calculation log · Troubleshooting

item.title: Calculation log
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Every calculation records its full basis, not just its answer. This is what makes a planning number defensible months after it was produced.

Open it by searching for Inventory Planning Calculation Log, or from the setup page, the worksheet, or Item Card → Inventory Planning → Calculation Log — which filters it to that item.

What each entry records

GroupFields
Identity Calculation type, item, date and time, user
Demand Average daily demand, standard deviation, observations, ADI, CV², demand pattern
Lead time Days, standard deviation, and the source the value came from
Safety stock inputs Service level applied, and the Z-score derived from it
EOQ inputs Annual demand, unit cost, holding cost, ordering cost
Outcome Raw result, final result, previous value, whether it was applied, result code, recommended policy, note

Calculation types

  • Safety Stock, Reorder Point, EOQ, Maximum Inventory — the four value calculators
  • Policy Advice — a demand classification and recommendation
  • Dynamic Supply — a value computed during a planning run by the optional dynamic provider, so planning-time values are as traceable as batch ones

Three questions it answers

“Why is this item's reorder point this number?”

Filter to the item, open the most recent Reorder Point entry. Average daily demand times lead time, plus safety stock — with every input listed, including which source the lead time came from.

“What was it before?”

The Previous Value field on every entry. You can reconstruct an item's whole planning history from the log.

“Why did nothing happen for this item?”

Entries are written even when no value is produced. The Result Code says which check stopped it and the Note explains — see Troubleshooting.

Set a retention policy

The log grows by one row per item per calculator per run.

A nightly run across 5,000 items writes roughly 25,000 rows a night. Set a retention policy.

The log is registered with the standard Business Central Retention Policy module, so this takes a minute:

  1. Search for Retention Policies
  2. New, and choose the table GSO Calculation Log
  3. Set a retention period — 90 days is a sensible start
  4. Enable the policy

Without a policy, nothing is ever deleted. Turning off Log Calculation History in setup stops the writes entirely, but you lose the audit trail — a retention policy is almost always the better answer.

Next: Troubleshooting · FAQ

item.title: Per-item controls
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Two fields on the Item Card Planning tab, for the items that need to differ from your company defaults.

Exclude from Inventory Planning

When ticked, the item is skipped by every calculator, every bulk run, every scheduled job and the dynamic provider. Nothing the app does will ever touch its planning values.

Use it for:

  • Items whose planning values a planner maintains deliberately, from knowledge the ledger does not contain
  • Items under a supplier agreement that fixes order quantities
  • Items in a launch or phase-out where history is actively misleading
  • Anything you have tuned by hand and do not want a nightly job to overwrite
This is the safety catch for scheduled runs.

A nightly job applies to every eligible item. If a value on an item matters to someone, tick this box rather than relying on nobody scheduling a run.

Planning Service Level % (0 = default)

A per-item service level for the safety stock calculation, overriding the company default in setup. Leave it at 0 to use the default. Range 70–99.99 when set.

This is how you do ABC-style differentiation without an ABC module:

ItemTypical levelReasoning
Critical lines — a stockout loses the order or stops production 98–99% The buffer is cheap relative to the consequence
Ordinary stock Company default (95%) Leave at 0
Low-value, easily substituted, or short shelf life 85–90% Carrying cost and obsolescence outweigh the odd stockout
Service level is not linear in cost.

Moving an item from 95% to 99% roughly doubles its safety stock. Raise it where a stockout is genuinely expensive, not across the board — otherwise you have simply bought more inventory.

Actions on the Item Card

The same tab carries the per-item calculator actions — Calculate All Planning Values, the four individual calculators, and a filtered view of the calculation log. See Running the calculators.

Bulk maintenance

Both fields are ordinary item fields, so they can be set for many items at once with the standard Edit in Excel action on the Item List, or through a configuration package.

Next: Running the calculators · Setup reference

item.title: Troubleshooting
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Every calculation carries a result code and a note. Start there — the app almost always tells you what stopped it.

Result codes

CodeMeaningWhat to do
OKCalculated and usableNothing
Cap AppliedUsable, but a configured cap limited the resultCheck Maximum EOQ (Months of Demand), or the item's Maximum Inventory for a capped reorder point
Insufficient Demand DataFewer days with demand than Min Demand ObservationsLengthen the history window, lower the minimum, or accept the item is too sporadic to model
Zero DemandNo demand at all in the windowNew item, dead item — or a manufacturing component with Count Consumption as Demand off
No Lead Time DataNo lead time from any sourceSet the item's Lead Time Calculation, or a fallback in setup
Item BlockedThe item is blockedExpected
Make-to-Order SkippedMake-to-order item, and skipping is onExpected — turn the setting off to include them
Not an Inventory ItemType is Service or Non-InventoryExpected
Excluded by Item SettingExclude from Inventory Planning is tickedExpected — untick it to include the item
Zero Unit CostEOQ needs a unit costPopulate the chosen cost source, or switch Unit Cost Source
Zero Ordering CostEOQ needs an ordering costSet Ordering Cost (S) in setup
Zero ResultThe formula produced zeroReported rather than written, so a real value is never replaced with nothing
ErrorUnexpected failureRead the note on the log entry, then contact support

Warnings in the note

Trend warning

Recent demand — the last quarter of the window, minimum 30 days — deviates from the full-window average by more than your threshold. History-based planning lags a ramp-up and overstates a phase-out. Consider a shorter window for fast-moving ranges, or set the values by hand and exclude the item.

Stockkeeping Unit notice

The item has Stockkeeping Units. Standard planning reads SKU values at a location, not the item card — so a value calculated here may appear to have no effect. This app calculates at item level by design.

Intermittent or lumpy demand warning

Safety stock rests on a normal approximation that does not really hold for this demand shape. The number is still the best available estimate, but it deserves review rather than trust.

Common situations

Every item reports Zero Demand

You manufacture, and Count Consumption as Demand is off. Components are consumed, never sold, so there is no sales history to find. Turn it on in setup.

Every item reports Insufficient Demand Data

Observations count days with demand, not transaction lines. An item with 200 sales lines across 12 busy days has 12 observations, and the default minimum is 20.

Lengthen the window or lower the minimum — but understand what you are agreeing to: a statistic from five days of demand is a statistic from five days of demand.

The calculated values are ignored by planning

Check for Stockkeeping Units on the item. Standard planning reads the SKU at a location rather than the item card. The calculation note says so whenever SKUs exist.

Also check the item's Reordering Policy. A reorder point on an item with no policy, or on Lot-for-Lot, does nothing.

The reorder point looks too low for a growing product

Read the note — there will be a trend warning. History-based planning lags growth by design.

EOQ returns Zero Unit Cost

The Unit Cost Source you chose is empty on that item. Populate it, or switch the source in setup to one your items actually carry.

Values changed and nobody knows why

Open the calculation log for the item. Every run records the previous value, the new value, the user, and every input that produced it.

A scheduled run overwrote values somebody had tuned

Tick Exclude from Inventory Planning on those items. Restore the old values from the Previous Value field in the log.

The results moved a lot after a setup change

Expected — the history window, service level, ordering cost and holding rate all feed the formulas directly. Use the Planning Worksheet to see the effect of a change before applying it anywhere.

Still stuck?

Contact support — we reply within 2 business days. Include the item number and a screenshot of the calculation log entry; that usually contains the whole answer.

The app is open source, so you can also read the calculation code or raise an issue at github.com/GmsoftLtd/bc-inventory-planning.

item.title: FAQ
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Formulas and methodology

What formula does safety stock use?

SS = Z × √( LT × σD² + D² × σLT² )

Where Z is the inverse normal at your service level, LT the lead time in days, σD the standard deviation of daily demand, D the average daily demand and σLT the standard deviation of lead time.

It covers variability in both demand and lead time. A simpler demand-only formula understates the buffer for items whose supplier is unreliable.

Where do the Z-scores come from?

A continuous inverse-normal approximation (Acklam), not a lookup table. A 94.9% service level gets a 94.9% buffer rather than being rounded down to the nearest tabulated bucket.

How is the reorder point calculated?

ROP = (average daily demand × lead time) + safety stock

Capped at the item's Maximum Inventory when one is set. The safety stock used is the freshly calculated one, not the value stored on the item.

How is EOQ calculated?

EOQ = √( 2 × D × S / H )

The Wilson formula, where D is annual demand, S the ordering cost, and H the annual holding cost per unit — unit cost multiplied by your holding rate. The result is capped at a configurable number of months of demand and reconciled with the item's Minimum Order Quantity, Maximum Order Quantity and Order Multiple.

How are demand patterns classified?

By the Syntetos–Boylan scheme, using ADI (how often demand occurs) and CV² (how variable the quantities are):

PatternADICV²Recommended policy
Smooth< 1.32< 0.49Fixed Reorder Qty.
Erratic< 1.32≥ 0.49Fixed Reorder Qty.
Intermittent≥ 1.32< 0.49Lot-for-Lot
Lumpy≥ 1.32≥ 0.49Lot-for-Lot

Two overrides come first: an item with an Expiration Calculation, or one that already has a Maximum Inventory, is steered to Maximum Qty. instead. Make-to-order items are recommended Order.

Both thresholds are configurable.

What counts as demand?

Sales, netted against same-day returns, measured across every calendar day in the history window. Days with no demand count toward the average, which is what makes the daily rate comparable with a lead time expressed in calendar days.

With Count Consumption as Demand enabled, production and assembly consumption count too.

How is lead time determined?

  1. Purchase receipt history — mean and standard deviation of order-to-receipt days from the trailing two years. The only source that also yields variability.
  2. The item's Lead Time Calculation — also used for produced and assembled items.
  3. The fallback you set in setup.

The source used is recorded on every log entry. Safety stock and reorder point share this resolution, so they cannot disagree.

Is this forecasting or AI?

No. It is descriptive statistics over posted history. That is deliberate: every number can be traced back to transactions you can open and check. The app tells you when history is a poor guide to the present — see the trend warning — rather than predicting around it.

Behaviour

Will it overwrite values my planners maintain?

Only if you let it. Tick Exclude from Inventory Planning on those items and no calculator, bulk run or scheduled job will touch them. You can also turn off any individual Write … to Item switch to calculate and log without writing at all.

Does it change my reordering policies?

Only with two separate opt-ins. Auto-Update Item Reordering Policy is off by default; recommendations are logged either way. And even when enabled, it never sets a policy of Order automatically.

Separately, Set Policy to Fixed Reorder Qty. when None gives a policy to items that have none, so a calculated reorder point does something. It is suppressed for any item whose advice recommends a different policy.

What happens if I uninstall the app?

The values it calculated stay on your items, because they live in standard Business Central fields. You lose the setup, the calculation log and the per-item controls.

Does it work per location?

No. It calculates at item level. When an item has Stockkeeping Units, standard planning reads the SKU values at a location rather than the item card — and the app says so explicitly in the calculation note, rather than leaving you to discover it.

Does it work in a demo or evaluation company?

Yes. History windows anchor to the work date, not the system date, so a company whose demo data sits in the past still produces real results. In production the two are the same.

Can I run different calculators on different schedules?

Yes. Create several Job Queue entries with different Parameter Strings — see Running the calculators.

Data and privacy

Does my data leave my tenant?

No. The app reads item ledger entries, purchase receipt lines and item master data, and writes to standard item planning fields plus its own setup and log tables. All of it stays in your environment.

What telemetry does the app collect?

Diagnostic events on the standard Business Central telemetry channel, sent to the publisher's Application Insights resource:

EventRaised whenData
GSO0001A scheduled run completesMode, item count
GSO0002An interactive bulk run completesCalculation type, item count
GSO0003The dynamic provider computes valuesEvent count only

These carry counts and codes only — never item numbers, quantities, costs, customer names or any other business data. Telemetry also flows to your own environment's Application Insights resource if you have configured one. See the privacy statement.
